title: FDA Approves First OTC Pill Combining Tylenol and Naproxen for 12-Hour Pain Relief
excerpt: The first-ever fixed-dose over-the-counter combination of acetaminophen and naproxen sodium offers up to 12 hours of non-opioid pain relief for adults and children 12 and older.
body:
• The FDA on July 24 approved Kenvue's Tylenol with Naproxen, the first OTC pill combining acetaminophen and naproxen sodium in a single dose.
  • Each dose contains 650 mg of acetaminophen and 220 mg of naproxen sodium, providing up to 12 hours of non-opioid pain relief.
  • Clinical studies across eight trials showed the combination delivered superior pain relief compared to either drug taken alone.
  • The FDA granted Kenvue three years of market exclusivity for the new formulation, which will soon be available at major U.S. retailers.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration on July 24 approved Tylenol with Naproxen, a new over-the-counter pain reliever that combines two widely used medications in a single tablet for the first time. The product, made by Kenvue, pairs acetaminophen — the active ingredient in Tylenol — with the anti-inflammatory drug naproxen sodium, offering up to 12 hours of pain relief without a prescription.

The non-opioid tablet is approved for adults and children aged 12 and older for temporary relief of headaches, back pain, muscle aches, toothaches, menstrual cramps, and minor pain from arthritis, according to the FDA.

How the Combination Works

Each dose contains 650 mg of acetaminophen and 220 mg of naproxen sodium. The two drugs target pain through different mechanisms: acetaminophen works quickly to reduce pain signals in the central nervous system, while naproxen sodium, a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), addresses pain associated with inflammation. The combination begins working in under 30 minutes, according to Kenvue.

https://x.com/Reuters/status/2080725422677840038

"The combination was evaluated across eight clinical studies and demonstrated superior pain relief compared to the individual medications."

— Michelle Bateson, Head of North America R&D, Kenvue

The product is the first and only fixed-dose combination of acetaminophen and naproxen sodium available without a prescription in the United States. The FDA granted Kenvue three years of exclusivity for the new formulation.

Market Impact and Kenvue's Position

Shares of Kenvue (KVUE) rose about 2% on the day of the announcement, according to Stocktwits. Tylenol is Kenvue's flagship pain-relief brand, generating roughly $1 billion in annual sales and accounting for about 8–10% of the company's total revenue. It anchors the company's Self Care segment, which delivered more than $6 billion in sales in 2025.

The approval comes at a transitional moment for Kenvue. The company, originally spun off from Johnson & Johnson, agreed in November 2025 to be acquired by Kimberly-Clark for more than $40 billion, according to Reuters. The transaction is expected to close later this year.

About 75% of persistent pain sufferers reported dissatisfaction with their current relief options, according to a March 2026 Kenvue survey of more than 6,200 people — a gap the company hopes the new combination product will address.

Political Context and Ongoing Legal Battles

The FDA said the approval aligns with President Donald Trump's "Great Healthcare Plan," a federal effort to make more verified safe pharmaceutical drugs available over the counter. The endorsement is notable given the Trump administration's fraught relationship with the Tylenol brand.

In September 2025, Trump and members of his administration claimed that acetaminophen use during pregnancy may be linked to autism, urging pregnant women to avoid the drug. The comments triggered a sharp drop in Kenvue's stock and drew widespread pushback from doctors, medical groups, and international health agencies, who said the science does not support a causal connection.

Kenvue has repeatedly stated that decades of evidence show Tylenol is safe when used as directed. Doctors and medical groups consider acetaminophen the preferred treatment for pain and fever during pregnancy, according to USA Today.

The controversy has also spilled into the courts. Texas sued Kenvue over alleged failures to warn pregnant consumers, and a U.S. appeals court this month revived more than 500 private lawsuits making similar claims, according to Reuters.

What This Means for Indian-Americans

For the Indian diaspora in the United States, the approval introduces a more convenient pain management option. Acetaminophen — known as paracetamol in India and much of the world — and naproxen are both familiar medications, but combining them in a single OTC dose is new. The 12-hour relief window could be particularly useful for those managing chronic conditions like arthritis or recurring back pain without wanting to juggle multiple pills or turn to prescription opioids.

Tylenol with Naproxen will be available soon at major U.S. retailers nationwide, Kenvue said, though specific pricing has not yet been announced.
